t: Tesla wants to buy assets of EMAG
d: Tesla notified Germany's Federal Cartel Office on 23 November 2026 of a planned acquisition of assets of the EMAG group, case B5-132/26, and the authority listed that review on 27 November 2026. The price and terms were not disclosed, and there is no clearance yet.

t: Tesla passes a thousand registered Cybercabs in Texas
d: Tesla registered a record 285 Cybercabs in Texas on Thanksgiving, 26 November 2026, the biggest one-day jump so far. The Texas roster now lists 1,107 Cybercabs, the first time that count has passed a thousand.

t: Tesla now leads German private EV switchers
d: Tesla took 10.1 percent of private German switches from a combustion car to a pure electric car in the first nine months of 2026, up from 4.5 percent a year earlier. HUK-COBURG's E-Barometer, published on 26 November 2026, puts the brand first for the first time.

t: Tesla cancels every Cybertruck reservation in Taiwan
d: On 26 November 2026 Tesla Taiwan told Cybertruck reservation holders that production will gradually stop and that their reservations are cancelled. The NT$3,000 deposit is refunded automatically, and a new Model 3 or Model Y on the same account can come with eight years of free Premium Connectivity.

t: Tesla nearly doubles its Dallas Robotaxi area
d: On 25 November 2026 Tesla's Robotaxi account posted a wider Dallas map and wrote that there are more cars and lower prices. Estimates traced from that map put the zone at about 150 square miles, up from about 81 to 82.

t: Neuralink gets FDA approval for pivotal ALS trial
d: On 25 November 2026 the FDA approved Neuralink to launch the LINK Pivotal Study in people with severe paralysis from ALS. The approval covers the trial and does not authorize sale of the implant.

t: SpaceX pledges one share per active Trump Account
d: On 25 November 2026 SpaceX said it will contribute one newly issued Class A share to every currently active Trump Account. The company says Elon Musk will match that number of shares, and Gwynne Shotwell has announced a separate personal gift of more than 2 million shares.

t: FCC authorizes one million Starmind data satellites
d: On 25 November 2026 the FCC Space Bureau granted SpaceX conditional authority for Starmind, up to 1 million low-Earth-orbit satellites that would work as orbital data centers. The first one must be operating by 25 November 2033.

t: Starlink Mini costs 99 dollars in the US
d: On 24 November 2026 Starlink cut the United States price of the Starlink Mini kit to 99 dollars, from a typical 249 dollars, and it is the lowest price the Mini has had. The kit is hardware only: a Roam plan and shipping are extra, and the Canadian kit has its own price.

t: Tesla raises the Cyberbeast price to $114,990
d: On 24 November 2026 Tesla raised the US Cyberbeast price by $5,000, from $109,990 to $114,990, before fees and taxes. It is the only Cybertruck trim a US buyer can still order new, and a new order is estimated as late as June 2027.

t: EU delays Tesla Assisted Driving meeting to mid-December
d: On 25 November 2026 a European Commission spokesperson told Reuters the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles will meet on 15 December to consider Tesla's bid for EU-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. The meeting had been set for 1 December, Flanders then put it on 7 December, and a vote is still not guaranteed.

t: Starlink gives up its US broadband subsidies
d: On 23 November 2026 the US NTIA published a zero-outlay BEAD model agreement, and SpaceX agreed to serve every awarded Starlink location at no cost to the program. Households still pay a monthly bill and only the customer equipment is free.

t: Tesla EU registrations rose 83.5 percent in October
d: Tesla registered 10,166 new cars in the EU in October 2026, up 83.5 percent from a year earlier, in ACEA figures published on 24 November 2026. Battery-electric cars took nearly 30 percent of the market that month, and BYD registered about three times as many cars as Tesla.

t: Five directors are negotiating the Tesla SpaceX merger
d: The Financial Times reported on 24 November 2026 that five directors, three from Tesla and two from SpaceX, are negotiating a possible combination worth about $3.5 trillion. The companies have not confirmed the names.

t: Tesla has its best day since April 2025
d: Tesla shares were up about 12% on 23 November 2026, trading around $387, and were on pace for the largest one-day percentage gain since 9 April 2025. The stock is still down about 13% for the year and about 20% below its record close.

t: Musk told SpaceX staff it lags in AI
d: On 23 November 2026 The New York Times reported that Elon Musk told SpaceX employees the company is falling behind in AI. Outlets relaying that report say Anthropic pays about $3.1 billion a month, and Google about $800 million, to rent SpaceX computing power.

t: Nvidia brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
d: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director on 23 November 2026, eleven days after he resigned. The board cited input from senior US government officials. Nvidia shares opened about 30% higher.

t: Two states sue SpaceX over Grok images
d: Virginia and Oregon filed the first US state lawsuits against SpaceX over Grok on 23 November 2026. The consumer-protection suits allege non-consensual sexualized images, including child sexual abuse material, and seek penalties, stricter guardrails and disgorgement.

t: Musk wants Starlink in every Tesla by 2027
d: On 22 November 2026 Elon Musk replied on X that an embedded Starlink option would hopefully be available towards the end of next year, a window that points to late 2027. He tied it to unsupervised FSD and said China is excluded because Starlink is illegal there.

t: SpaceX relaunched from one pad after 32 hours
d: SpaceX flew two Falcon 9 rockets from SLC-4E at Vandenberg 32 hours, 3 minutes and 21 seconds apart, its fastest turnaround from one pad. NROL-136 lifted off on 22 November 2026 after USSF-317 on 20 November.

t: Neuralink enrolled 21 people in its trials
d: On 28 January 2026 Neuralink said 21 people were enrolled in its trials worldwide. Reuters reported the same figure the same day. The company also said it had no serious device-related adverse events.

t: Tesla taped out the AI5 chip design
d: On 15 April 2026 Elon Musk said Tesla's team had taped out the AI5 chip. Electrek and TechNode both reported the post. Tape-out sends a finished design to be manufactured.

t: Tesla shut down the Dojo training computer
d: In August 2025 Bloomberg reported that Tesla was disbanding the Dojo team. Musk then said Dojo 2 was an evolutionary dead end and that the work would focus on AI5 and AI6.

t: A household socket supplies about 1300 watts
d: Tesla's Gen 2 Mobile Connector manual rates the ordinary household adapter at 1.3 kW on a 120-volt socket. Electrek reported the same 1.3 kW ceiling.

t: New Teslas lost the included mobile charger
d: Tesla stopped including the Mobile Connector with new orders after 17 April 2022 and sold the cable separately. Musk cited low use.

t: Tesla's wall charger also fits other cars
d: Tesla's Universal Wall Connector charges NACS cars and, with a built-in J1772 adapter, other electric cars. Its top output is 11.5 kW.

t: Tesla started Semi deliveries in Nevada
d: On 24 September 2026 Tesla handed Semi trucks to customers from its factory in Sparks, Nevada. It still did not publish a price or a delivery count.

t: Neuralink participant plays GTA VI with his mind
d: On 20 November 2026 Neuralink posted a video of about two minutes in which a clinical-trial participant plays GTA VI with his brain implant, one day after the game’s worldwide release. The implants remain investigational and are not approved by the FDA or other regulators.

t: HSBC more than doubles its Tesla price target
d: On 20 November 2026 HSBC analyst Michael Tyndall upgraded Tesla to Hold from Reduce and raised the price target to $359 from $157, about 129 percent higher, on a possible SpaceX combination. The new target is still below Tesla's close of $374.41 on 19 November.

t: Tesla starts rolling out FSD v15 to testers
d: On 21 November 2026 Tesla said on X that FSD (Supervised) v15 is starting to roll out, first to Early Access Program members in software update 2026.38.6.11. Tesla claims 25 times better handling of safety-critical cases, a figure that is not independently verified, and the driver still has to pay attention.

t: Himes threatens SpaceX funding over Ukraine Starshield slowdowns
d: On 20 November 2026 Jim Himes asked Elon Musk to explain October Starshield slowdowns in Ukraine, and wrote that supporting funding for SpaceX-developed government systems is difficult until those answers arrive. No funding restriction has been imposed.

t: Nvidia fell 14 percent after Anthropic's debut
d: On 20 November 2026, one day after Anthropic's record listing, Nvidia lost about 14 percent and the Nasdaq 5.3 percent. Anthropic, Tesla and SpaceX all fell too.

t: Italy approves Tesla Assisted Driving before the EU
d: Italy's transport ministry gave provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for FSD (Supervised), on 20 November 2026. Italy is the 12th European country to allow it and the first large EU market.

t: Investors funded 44 billion dollars of SpaceX chips
d: Apollo and Goldman Sachs priced about 44 billion dollars of notes on 20 November 2026 to buy Nvidia Vera Rubin chips that SpaceX will lease. It is the largest GPU financing so far, and the chips arrive in the first half of 2027.

t: Tesla now sells cars in Argentina
d: Tesla launched in Argentina on 20 November 2026 with the Model 3 and Model Y, sold online from 41,590 dollars. The first showroom is in a shopping centre north of Buenos Aires, and the first cars reach buyers in March or April 2027.

t: Anthropic made the biggest stock debut ever
d: Anthropic sold shares at 83 dollars and started trading on Nasdaq as ANT on 19 November 2026. With the extra shares the banks bought, the listing raised about 93.5 billion dollars, more than any IPO before it.

t: Tesla wants to make solar silicon in Texas
d: Tesla has applied for a Texas school-tax break for a 3.1 billion dollar plant that would make solar-grade polysilicon from 2030. The application says Tesla would not build it in Texas without the break.

t: SpaceX Caught Starship After 22 Hours
d: On Flight 15, SpaceX caught the Starship ship 22 hours and 32 minutes after liftoff. The booster's catch was aborted over the Gulf. The 22-hour figure is SpaceX's own timeline.

t: DeepSeek opens its chat tools
d: DeepSeek said on 13 November 2026 that a full set of application APIs is available on deepseek-flash, and that a demo chat client is open source.

t: Meta releases small model Muse Ember
d: Meta released Muse Ember on 9 November 2026 and called it the smallest and most efficient model for tool calls, short coding tasks, routing and extraction.

t: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
d: Alibaba Cloud unveiled Qwen4-Max in Hangzhou on 16 November 2026. The company says it has 2.4 trillion parameters and a 1 million token context.

t: Anthropic starts its stock roadshow
d: Anthropic said on 10 November 2026 that it has started the roadshow for a listing. The expected price range is 70 to 78 dollars a share.

t: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2
d: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on 9 November 2026. They are the same underlying model, with different access rules.

t: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon
d: Google said on 10 November 2026 that Gemini 4 Carbon is available to developers, companies, scientists and consumers.

t: Starlink's new satellites are raising their orbits
d: All 26 Starlink V3 satellites launched on Starship Flight 15 are healthy and have started climbing toward their working orbits, Starlink engineering lead Michael Nicolls said on 14 November 2026.

t: Grok Bot 1.0 now joins whole teams
d: SpaceXSI launched Grok Bot 1.0 on 11 November 2026. Shared bots can enter Slack, Microsoft Teams and video calls, and the company says they can offer to take on work.

t: Boring expects Nashville riders in early 2027
d: In a 17 November 2026 interview, Boring Company CEO Steve Davis said he expects the first mile of the Music City Loop to carry passengers in the first quarter of 2027. That is his bet, not an opening date.

t: Neuralink opens a US trial after stroke
d: Neuralink’s PRIME2 study, posted on ClinicalTrials.gov on 10 November 2026, is recruiting adults with spinal cord injury, ALS, or chronic ischemic stroke. The registry lists no implants and no results yet.

t: United now flies Starlink on most flights
d: United said on 12 November 2026 that Starlink Wi-Fi is on more than half of its daily flights, with nearly 64 percent expected by the end of 2026. The service is free for MileagePlus members.

t: Researchers found thousands of open Grok apps
d: Security firm Claroc told Ars Technica it found more than 35,000 public Grok apps, including 24 built inside SpaceXSI. Grok said the report confused grok.com’s app builder with Grok Build.

t: A third Boring machine has reached Nashville
d: The Nashville Business Journal reported on 17 November 2026 that The Boring Company’s third tunnel machine has arrived and is preparing to launch from Murfreesboro Pike. The company has not said it is digging.

t: One Neuralink user reached 75 words a minute
d: On 28 October 2026 Neuralink said one participant with ALS reached 75 words a minute in the first week, at a 5.8 percent word error rate. The figure is the company’s own report, not a paper.

t: Neuralink built speech tools in 72 hours
d: On 29 October 2026 Neuralink described a 72-hour visit to the home of one VOICE participant, where engineers prototyped hands-free speech tools and tested them with him. The devices remain investigational.

t: Spaceballs named Insane and Plaid
d: Tesla's fastest Model S modes run from Insane in 2014 to Ludicrous in 2015, a hidden Ludicrous+ in 2017 and Plaid in 2021. Ludicrous and Plaid come from a 1987 Mel Brooks comedy, and the speed that film put past ludicrous became a 1,020-horsepower car.

t: One door delayed Model X by two years
d: The falcon wing door was supposed to be better than any other door. It helped push the Model X almost two years late, sent Tesla to court against its supplier, and led the company to blame its own hubris.

t: SpaceX catches a Starship for the first time
d: SpaceX has caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time. Ship 42 flew for 22.5 hours on Flight 15 before the Starbase tower's arms closed around it; the booster's catch was called off.

t: Super Heavy does not return after a splashdown
d: Starship's Super Heavy booster can hover gently over the Gulf, yet every one that went into the sea was lost. Here is what happens after splashdown, and why only a tower catch brings a booster back.

t: Super Heavy skipped the tower on Flight 15
d: On Flight 15 Starship reached orbit, but Super Heavy skipped the tower and splashed into the Gulf. Here is how SpaceX decides whether a booster gets caught, and why the sea is the default.

t: Launch damage made SpaceX skip the booster catch
d: On Flight 6 a Super Heavy booster was minutes from the second tower catch ever when the launch itself damaged the tower. Why SpaceX sent the booster into the sea instead, and how that caution paid off.

t: Catching the ship takes about 22 hours
d: On Flight 15 SpaceX plans to catch the Super Heavy booster after about 6.5 minutes and the ship about 22.5 hours later, at the same tower. Here is why the ship has to wait almost a whole day.

t: The flying Roadster still took nine years
d: In 2017 Elon Musk called flying cars noisy and dangerous; that same year he unveiled a Roadster that would end up flipping in midair. The story of the thruster tweet, nine years of slipped dates and the flight.

t: Fans and nitrogen thrusters would lift the Roadster
d: The new Tesla Roadster drove upside down and flipped over a Semi. Here is how its suction fans and SpaceX-style nitrogen thrusters do it, and why it can only stay up for seconds.

t: Six stations grew into 85000 plugs
d: In 2012 Tesla opened six solar-powered chargers and promised Model S owners free charging forever. Here is how that network crossed a continent, opened to rivals, survived the firing of almost its entire team, and became the hardest part of Tesla to copy.

t: Each Tesla battery holds thousands of small cells
d: The first Tesla ran on 6,831 laptop cells; a Cybertruck stores twice the energy in 1,344. Why Tesla builds packs from small cylinders, what makes the 4680 different, and whether it matters when you buy.

t: Starship's first flight ended in a crater
d: In April 2023 Starship's first flight lasted four minutes, wrecked its own launch pad and had to be blown up. This is how that failure set up the attempt to catch both halves of the rocket.

t: Washers and lasers keep Robotaxi cameras clear
d: A Robotaxi has no driver to wipe a dirty lens. Here is how Tesla keeps its cameras clean today, what its 'eyelid' and laser patents describe, and what it means for owners.

t: Mr Steven chased falling nose cones for SpaceX
d: For almost three years SpaceX tried to catch falling Falcon 9 nose cones in a giant net on a boat. It finally worked in 2019, then the company gave it up. The story explains why, and what it means for catching Starship.

t: Starship uses 33 engines instead of one
d: The Soviet N1 failed with 30 engines and Apollo's giant F-1 took years to tame. Here is why SpaceX's Super Heavy uses 33 Raptors, and why it works where the N1 did not.

t: SpaceX landed its first orbital rocket in 2015
d: In 2015 SpaceX crashed two boosters on its landing ship and lost a whole rocket before a Falcon 9 first stage finally flew back and landed upright in Florida. The story of that first landing, and why it still matters for Starship.

t: Here is what one kilo to orbit costs
d: The fuel for a Starship flight works out to about 9 dollars a kilo, yet the Space Shuttle cost about 54,500. Here is why, how Falcon 9 cut the price, and what Starship needs to get under 100 dollars a kilo.

t: The Semi driver sits in a center seat
d: Inside the Tesla Semi: the center seat, the two 16-inch screens, the jump seat and the missing bed, and how charging fits a driver's legal breaks in the US and Europe.

t: Your Tesla still needs support after production ends
d: Tesla is ending the Cybertruck after the Model S and X. What that means for warranty, parts, service, software updates and resale value, with lessons from the original Roadster.

t: The Cybertruck broke its own window
d: From a cracked window on stage in 2019 to the end of production at Giga Texas: the story of the stainless steel bet behind the Cybertruck, what it cost Tesla and what it leaves behind.

t: Starship fires its engines at its own booster
d: Starship lights its six engines while it is still attached to the Super Heavy booster. Here is how hot staging works, why it adds payload, who did it first and what it means for catching both stages.

t: A tent saved Tesla from production hell
d: In June 2018, close to running out of money, Tesla built a whole Model 3 assembly line in a tent on its parking lot. How it happened, whether it worked, and why it still shapes how Tesla builds cars.

t: Today's rules block a Cybercab without a wheel
d: Tesla's Cybercab is touring Europe, but nobody can ride it. How European type approval works, why driverless cars are capped at 1,500 a year, and what has to change first.

t: First Starlinks left the rocket stacked like cards
d: In 2019 SpaceX stacked 60 flat satellites in one rocket and simply let them drift apart. The story of the rushed bet that became the blueprint for every Starlink launch, and why it matters to Tesla.

t: SpaceX catches Starship without wings or legs
d: SpaceX wants to catch both Starship stages with its launch tower. How a ship without wings falls belly first, flips upright and lands in the tower's arms, why that is harder than catching the booster, and how it lands on the Moon instead.

t: The Tesla Semi needed nine years to arrive
d: Promised for 2019 with 500 miles of range and sports-car acceleration, the Tesla Semi was delayed by battery shortages, proved its range in a 1,076-mile day and now heads for Europe. The story of the truck, and the one promise still open.

t: The Tesla phone remains a rumor
d: Viral videos promise a solar-charged Tesla Model Pi with Starlink built in. Here is what Tesla and Musk have actually said, how Starlink is coming to ordinary phones instead, and how to spot a fake.

t: SpaceX caught a booster using giant chopsticks
d: Super Heavy was built without landing legs, betting everything on a tower that could catch it in midair. How the idea was born, how the first catch in October 2024 worked, and why it matters for every Starship flight since.

t: Sleeping while FSD drives is still not allowed
d: Grok can plan your route and Tesla FSD can drive it, but you may not sleep at the wheel. What each system does, why napping is not allowed yet, and when it could be.

t: The Lotus that became the first Tesla
d: Tesla's first car was meant to be a quick electric conversion of a Lotus Elise. In the end only about 7% of the Lotus survived, the costs exploded, and the Roadster still started everything Tesla is today.

t: One accidental tap reportedly cost 539 dollars
d: A month after launch, a Model Y driver in Austin drove off a Supercharger with the cable attached, and an owner who never moved the car was reportedly told it costs $539 to clear the alert.

t: FSD Supervised still needs you at the wheel
d: Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) explained: what the system really does, why you must keep watching, the monthly price in the US, UK, Europe and Australia, and the countries where it is allowed as of October 2026.

t: Tesla halves the China deposit to 39900 yuan
d: Until November 30, Chinese buyers can finance a Model 3, Model Y or Model Y L over five years at 0% with half the usual down payment, as Tesla's sales in China keep falling.

t: Italy backs EU-wide approval of Tesla FSD
d: Italy's transport minister says Rome supports a swift EU approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. With Germany already on board, Tesla now has a path past the EU's population rule, but only just.

t: Robotaxi service now runs until 2 am
d: Tesla's driverless ride service now operates from 6 a.m. to 2 a.m., 20 hours a day. The update also adds features aimed at night riders, but Tesla has not said which cities get the new hours.

t: Cybercab's battery is ready for cheaper LFP cells
d: Tesla engineers told Munro Live that the Cybercab's pack has spare room for cheaper LFP cells, is split into four replaceable modules, and that the body is coloured without paint. Optimus may soon plug the robotaxis in.

t: Owners chose 36 new Supercharger sites
d: Tesla named 36 owner-voted Supercharger locations on October 28, from Cannon Beach to Lossiemouth, and opened a new voting round. Here is where they are, how voting works and why winners do not open overnight.

t: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 in Hayward
d: A Tesla Semi burst into flames on a Bay Area freeway on Tuesday evening without hitting anything. The driver was unhurt, but the cause is still unknown, just as Semi volume production ramps up.

t: Houston's Robotaxi zone is now ten times larger
d: Tesla's driverless Model Y service in Houston now covers about 254 square miles, from the northwest suburbs through downtown, while its registered robotaxi fleet in Texas tops 1,000 cars.

t: Latvia approves FSD as the EU's tenth country
d: Latvia has recognized the Dutch approval for Tesla Assisted Driving, yet the ten approving countries hold only about 14% of EU residents. Here is why an EU-wide yes in December needs Germany, France, Italy or Spain.

t: South Korean police book 80 Tesla owners
d: Seoul police seized 21 plug-in modules used to switch on FSD in Teslas not approved for it. Most Korean Teslas, including every Shanghai-built Model 3 and Model Y, still cannot legally use the feature.

t: Japan cuts EV subsidies 40% from 2027
d: Japan's trade ministry is shrinking its clean-car grants for cars registered from January 1, 2027. A Tesla Model Y or Model 3 drops from ¥1.27 million to ¥762,000, setting up a year-end rush in one of Tesla's fastest-growing markets.

t: A Barclays upgrade lifts Tesla shares 5.2%
d: Barclays analyst Dan Levy raised Tesla to Overweight and lifted his price target to $450 from $370, calling a SpaceX merger a key part of the bull case. The stock closed Monday at $391.62, but any deal still faces a tough shareholder vote.

t: Turo will offer FSD rentals in the US
d: Turo is linking to Tesla's systems to verify which rental Teslas have Full Self-Driving (Supervised) active, giving Tesla a new way to put FSD in front of people who have never tried it.

t: Humanoid robots now have a first safety standard
d: Humanoid robots like Optimus do not fit existing robot safety rules, because they fall over when they lose power. A new ISO standard, still in draft, is meant to fix that.

t: Cybercab is the vehicle behind Robotaxi rides
d: Robotaxi and Cybercab are often used as if they mean the same thing, but they don't. Robotaxi is Tesla's ride-hailing service; the Cybercab is one of the cars that drives in it. Here is the difference, in plain terms.

t: Cybercabs ferried F1 fans around Austin
d: Driverless Cybercabs carried race fans to the Circuit of the Americas this weekend. Trackers logged a record 1,250 sightings on qualifying day, and Texas now lists 463 Cybercabs, though Tesla has not said how many rides it gave.

t: Musk unveils Terafab in Austin
d: At a livestreamed keynote in Austin, Elon Musk announced Terafab, a joint chip-making project of Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. It starts with an 'advanced technology fab' that can make logic and memory chips and their masks under one roof, and makes two kinds of chips: one for Optimus and cars, one for AI in space.

t: Tesla app code hints at Optimus at home
d: Hidden strings in recent Tesla app versions suggest Tesla is preparing owners' phones for Optimus: a consent screen for home video data, robot alerts, and Optimus listed as an energy site with charger IDs.

t: Musk says Optimus and Cybercab will dominate Tesla
d: Replying to a post on X, Elon Musk said Tesla's humanoid robot and its robotaxi will make up most of the company's value. Meanwhile, the new Roadster already borrows actuators from Optimus.

t: Musk promises an Optimus video without a script
d: On Tesla's Q3 2026 call, Musk said a new Optimus video showing tasks that were not pre-programmed is coming within a month or two. Tesla's past demos explain why the claim will be closely watched.

t: Optimus deliveries to outsiders wait until late 2027
d: On its Q3 2026 earnings call, Tesla said the first production-quality Optimus robots are coming off a Fremont line. Deliveries to other companies are now expected around the end of 2027.

t: Cybercab passengers can now see the road behind
d: Passengers in Austin's Cybercabs can now open the rear and side cameras during a ride, and a dark-screen quiet mode has appeared too. The update lands just ahead of Tesla's October 30 deadline to answer NHTSA's questions on mirrors and rear-view cameras.

t: Model 3 and Y now supply home backup
d: Tesla has extended Powershare home backup to new Model 3 and Model Y cars in the US, but only in homes with a Powerwall 3 and a Wall Connector. The car can add more than two days of power to the home battery.

t: Powerwall 2 owners can now add Powerwall 3
d: A software update now lets Powerwall 2 systems in North America and Australia add a Powerwall 3 and up to three expansion units. Here is what you need, what is not supported and how far a system can grow.

t: Tesla Powerwall 3 goes on sale in Japan
d: Tesla has started selling the Powerwall 3 home battery in Japan. The 13.5 kWh unit delivers 9.69 kW, is registered for government subsidies and should be installed from September or October.

t: Two Powerwalls lease for 35 dollars a month
d: Tesla Electric now offers Texans a lease on two Powerwalls with no installation cost, at about $35 a month after a bill credit, if they sign up for its Backup electricity plan. Here is how the deal works and what the catches are.

t: Tesla cuts Powerwall lease prices in two states
d: Tesla now offers cheaper, no-money-down Powerwall leases in Massachusetts and Connecticut that come with automatic virtual power plant enrolment. In return, Tesla can dispatch the batteries 70 to 100 times a year.

t: A Tesla merger still needs Musk's personal approval
d: SpaceX's third-quarter 10-Q lists three approvals for a combination with Tesla: its special committee, its board and its controlling shareholder, Elon Musk. Here is what that means for Tesla shareholders.

t: A Dutch Powerwall changes when net metering ends
d: Dutch net metering ends on 1 January 2027, and Tesla now sells both the Powerwall 3 and the three-phase Powerwall 3P in the Netherlands. Here is what changes, what a battery can realistically save and when it makes sense.

t: Fans and thrusters sit inside the new Roadster
d: In a detailed walkaround, Tesla engineering chief Lars Moravy explained what sits under the Roadster's skin: two rear motors with over a megawatt, an aluminium-can 4680 battery, Optimus actuators, four suction fans and a 10,000 psi nitrogen system built with SpaceX.

t: New Teslas in Japan can power external devices
d: Tesla Japan has launched updated Model 3 and Model Y cars that can power appliances, plus a CHAdeMO adapter that unlocks about 14,000 extra fast chargers. A discount worth up to ¥264,000 goes to the first 5,000 buyers.

t: Doug Field joins Rivian's robot rival Mind
d: Doug Field, who led engineering for the Tesla Model 3 launch, is the new president of Mind Robotics, the factory-robot company spun out of Rivian. Mind has raised more than $1 billion and deliberately avoids copying the human body. Here is how it compares with Tesla Optimus.

t: Cybercab's assembly chief leaves for Rivian
d: Jody Kerns, who ran Cybercab final assembly at Giga Texas, is joining Rivian to lead R2 assembly in Illinois. He is the second key Cybercab launch manager to leave Tesla this year.

t: Ferrari's CEO gives Tesla's Roadster launch a 10
d: Speaking at an Italian auto conference on Tuesday, Ferrari chief executive Benedetto Vigna praised the technology and presentation of Tesla's new Roadster, and thanked Tesla for showing that an old industry can still dare to innovate.

t: Tesla still offers no Hardware 3 upgrade
d: A shareholder question asking when HW3 owners will learn about a free upgrade for unsupervised FSD was among the most-voted, but Tesla did not read it out. Here is what Tesla has said about HW3 so far, and why the silence matters.

t: NHTSA proposes optional cyan lights for driverless cars
d: The US safety regulator wants to let self-driving cars carry up to eight steady cyan lamps that show no human is watching the road, and to drop steering-wheel-based lighting rules for cars without manual controls. Here is what the proposal says and what it means for Tesla.

t: Tesla turns Superchargers into FSD showrooms
d: A sign at a Supercharger in Mississauga, Ontario, invites drivers to try FSD (Supervised). It is a shift from earlier Supercharger events that were about selling cars, and it targets the many Tesla owners who have never tried FSD.

t: Tesla closes the rear-screen browser trick
d: A popular workaround let rear passengers reach a web browser through YouTube and stream services Tesla Theater does not offer. Update 2026.38 shuts it down. Here is what changed and what still works.

t: A Cybercab loses a door panel in Philadelphia
d: Photos from South Broad Street show a gold Cybercab with its driver-side door skin torn off after a low-speed collision. It is unclear who was at fault or who was driving. The crash confirms that Tesla is testing Cybercabs in Pennsylvania, where it has no self-driving permit.

t: Tesla pauses Model 3 Premium orders in Canada
d: The Shanghai-built Model 3 Premium, which started at C$39,490, has disappeared from Tesla's Canadian configurator. Tesla says it has used up its import allocation, yet government data shows most of the national quota is still unused.

t: Other Tesla models fall 48% in Q3
d: Tesla delivered 8,295 vehicles outside the Model 3 and Model Y in the third quarter, the lowest since 2021. With the Model S and X gone, the Cybertruck makes up most of that figure, and it is still far below Tesla's original plans.

t: Former Optimus chief Kovac joins Boston Dynamics
d: Milan Kovac, who led Tesla's Optimus humanoid robot programme until June 2025, has been appointed adviser and outside director at Boston Dynamics. The move strengthens one of Optimus's most direct rivals just after Atlas was shown at CES 2026.

t: Vegas Loop heads for Paradise Road and UNLV
d: The Boring Company's Las Vegas network now has 14 stations and is digging towards Virgin Hotels and the UNLV area, with a target of November's Formula 1 race. How it fits the 1,200-Tesla plan.

t: Map update NA-2026.38 is now rolling out
d: Just two months after the last one, Tesla has started sending a new map package to cars in North America. It brings fresher roads, speed limits and lane guidance, and installs silently over Wi-Fi.

t: Q3 adds 1.2 billion to the warranty reserve
d: Tesla's quarterly SEC filing shows it sharply raised its estimates for warranty costs on cars already sold, handed back $475 million of regulatory credit revenue and still holds $4.08 billion in deferred revenue for FSD and other features.

t: Premium Connectivity adds features for a fee
d: Standard Connectivity is free for eight years; Premium costs $9.99, £9.99 or €9.99 a month. What each tier includes, how trials and lifetime Premium work, and when paying makes sense.

t: UK police reopen a Grok deepfake case
d: South Wales Police have reopened the case of a woman whose explicit Grok-generated image was posted on X, now under sexual offences law. A week earlier, Ofcom set out what X and SpaceXAI have changed. Here is where things stand, and the link to Tesla.

t: Tesla has never named a successor to Musk
d: Tesla has never named a successor, but Musk must deliver a CEO succession framework to earn the last two tranches of his 2025 award. How Tesla's succession process works, and what the filings allow.

t: Tesla data shows driver-assist in a fatal crash
d: A 2021 Model Y crossed the median of Route 55 in Vineland in August and hit an SUV head-on, killing its 68-year-old driver. Police said the Tesla 'lost control'; Tesla's federal crash report now marks its driver assistance as verified engaged.

t: A Cybercab's first reported crash was a pothole
d: Federal crash data show the first reported incident involving Tesla's Cybercab: a low-speed drive into a water-filled pothole in August, with a safety monitor aboard and no one hurt. Here is what the report says, and why it is not in Tesla's own safety numbers.

t: Tesla launches a Certified Pre-Owned program
d: Used Teslas sold through the new program get a check of more than 115 points, a one-year or 10,000-mile warranty and a history report. It is available in the US and Puerto Rico, not yet in Canada or Europe.

t: Starlink prices rose again in 2026
d: Starlink raised most monthly plans by $5 to $10 in 2026 while hardware got cheaper. Current prices for home and Roam plans, the extra fees, and what it means for Tesla owners using a Starlink Mini.

t: The Cybercab uses half as many parts
d: On Tesla's Q3 2026 call, engineering chief Lars Moravy said the Cybercab has about 50% fewer parts than any car Tesla has built, and that test bursts show the Texas line can beat its listed capacity. Regulators, not the factory, may set the pace.

t: Nevada lawmakers question Vegas Loop safety
d: A legislative hearing put The Boring Company's Las Vegas tunnels under scrutiny over worker injuries and environmental violations. The facts, both sides, and why it matters for the Tesla-powered Loop.

t: Tesla wants a Supercharger above the Arctic Circle
d: Town documents show Tesla has asked Inuvik to host two to four Supercharger stalls on town land, for $200 a month. It would be the first Supercharger in the Northwest Territories, about 2,700 km from Canada's current northernmost site.

t: Model 3 and Model Y fit different buyers
d: The Model Y costs $1,500 to $3,000 more than the equivalent Model 3 but offers far more cargo space. A side-by-side guide to prices in the US and Europe, range, performance and the cheaper Standard versions.

t: Tesla wants thousands of Optimus robots training together
d: Tesla has no fleet of robots collecting data the way its cars do. Its answer is the 'Optimus Academy', where 10,000 to 20,000 robots would practise tasks and feed what they learn into the next AI model. Here is what Tesla said, and what is still unclear.

t: Twitter-fraud claims against Musk close in November
d: A jury found two of Musk's 2022 tweets misled Twitter investors, and a judge largely upheld the verdict. Where the case stands, who can claim, and its links to Musk's Tesla share sales.

t: Giga Shanghai builds its 6 millionth battery pack
d: Tesla's Shanghai factory has assembled six million battery packs. The last million took about nine months, as exports from the plant hit records while sales inside China fall. Here is what the milestone shows about Tesla's biggest factory.

t: Tesla shares finish earnings week up 4.9%
d: Tesla shares closed Friday at $372.22, up 4.9% for the week. Three straight gains ahead of the Q3 report and the SpaceX merger committee news were followed by two down days after the earnings call.

t: Tesla cancels the Cybertruck in Australia and NZ
d: Tesla is refunding Cybertruck deposits in Australia and New Zealand and offering a free year of FSD instead. The move suggests a right-hand-drive Cybertruck, including for the UK, is not coming.

t: Staff still plug in Austin Robotaxis by hand
d: A video from Austin shows ten empty Tesla Robotaxis, including a Cybercab, parking themselves at a Supercharger while one employee plugs them in. It is a stopgap until Tesla's wireless charging hubs are ready.

t: Robovan could carry crowds through the Vegas Loop
d: The Boring Company's president says the 20-seat Robovan would handle event surges at Allegiant Stadium and the Sphere after the network is fully built. What is planned, and what is still uncertain.

t: SpaceX launches Google's first AI-in-space satellite
d: SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare carried 130 payloads, including the first prototype for Google's Project Suncatcher, which will test Google's AI chips in orbit. Here is what Google is trying, how it compares with SpaceX's own plans, and the Tesla angle.

t: Starlink Mobile passes 22 million users
d: SpaceX's direct-to-phone service grew 37% in a quarter, mostly through partner carriers. What VEON's 11 million users and Rogers' expansion show, and what it could mean for connected Teslas.

t: Giga Berlin built 7000 Model Ys that week
d: Tesla says its plant in Grünheide near Berlin has produced 7,000 Model Ys in one week, up from the 6,000 mark it first reached in 2024. The target is 7,500 a week. Here is what the milestone means and what it does not tell us.

t: Canadian companies can now buy their own Superchargers
d: Tesla has launched Supercharger for Business and Semi Charging for Business in Canada. Companies buy at least four V4 posts, or two truck chargers, set their own prices and leave the servicing to Tesla.

t: Inspect the car closely on Tesla delivery day
d: A practical guide to collecting a new Tesla in the US, UK or Europe: the app steps before the day, an exterior and interior checklist, and how to report problems.

t: Musk has spent years fighting the SEC
d: How Musk's two biggest SEC cases ended, why he is no longer Tesla's chairman, and what the 2026 settlement over his Twitter stake does and does not change for Tesla.

t: App 4.62 adds rewards for FSD referrals
d: The new Tesla app version is best known for its tablet layout, but its code also points to an FSD referral program, X Money as a way to pay for Supercharging and FSD, and the option to share a Wall Connector with up to five people.

t: Tesla recovers Cybertruck tooling from Angstrom
d: A federal judge has given Tesla the right to enter supplier Angstrom Automotive's closing plant in Troy, Texas, and take back the dies and casting tools it needs to build the Cybertruck. A flyover the next day suggested production is recovering.

t: Falcon Heavy flies its first spy satellite mission
d: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy launched the classified NROL-97 mission for the National Reconnaissance Office, its 14th flight. The two side boosters landed back at Cape Canaveral. Here are the details, and why this rocket is forever linked to Tesla.

t: Robotaxi code hints owners can add their cars
d: A teardown of Tesla Robotaxi app version 26.10 found code for enrolling privately owned Teslas in the ride-hailing network, chosen by VIN. It also reveals rider features such as AR car finding and rear-seat controls. Nothing is confirmed yet.

t: Tesla still holds bitcoin worth 962 million
d: Tesla has not bought or sold bitcoin since 2022, but under fair-value accounting its remaining coins now move its quarterly profit. Here is how much it holds, what it is worth after Q3 2026 and why it matters.

t: Tesla audits Chinese suppliers for Optimus Gen 3
d: A Tesla team is reportedly checking production lines at Chinese parts makers in Ningbo, Hangzhou and Shanghai before mass production of the third-generation Optimus robot. Cost per unit is a key focus. Here is what is reported, and what is not confirmed.

t: Tesla owes 161700 Canadian dollars after the fire
d: A Quebec judge refused to reopen a default judgment against Tesla Canada over a 2020 Model X that caught fire while being driven, saying the company's claim that fires usually come from misuse was backed by no data.

t: Update 2026.32 quietly adds a browser ad blocker
d: Tesla's release notes never tell the whole story. Update 2026.32 quietly adds an ad blocker to the car's browser, switches seat heaters off after 20 minutes and lets you see whether your Model 3 or Model Y supports Powershare.

t: The new Roadster can perform some stunts itself
d: A new Tesla video shows the Roadster's cockpit software, from aero settings to a thruster pressure readout. Musk says owners will be able to let the car perform its stunts autonomously, and promises a looping test track in Texas.

t: Each Vegas Loop mile costs several million dollars
d: A Boring Company executive has shared rare figures on cost, ridership and digging speed. What they show about the Tesla-powered tunnel network, and what they leave out.

t: New X subscription bundles Grok from 8 dollars
d: Musk's AI company has merged its consumer plans into one X Subscription with five tiers, from free to $200 a month. Here are the prices, what each tier includes, and how it relates to the Grok features in Tesla cars.

t: Starlink will lower 4400 satellites to 480 km
d: SpaceX says a lower orbit means dead satellites fall back within months instead of years. The reasons behind the move, the December debris incident, and the link to Tesla.

t: Tesla's Wall Connector gets smart charging
d: A firmware update for Powerwall and the Gen 3 Wall Connector lets your home battery decide when your EV charges, either when electricity is cheapest or when the panels produce more than the house needs. Here is how it works and what you need.

t: Tesla Energy has 10.7 billion dollars in orders
d: Tesla's Q3 2026 filing shows long-term energy contracts worth $10.73 billion still to be delivered, and customer prepayments that jumped by almost $1 billion in three months. Here is what those numbers say about Megapack demand.

t: Anthropic rents all of Colossus 1
d: SpaceX's AI unit will hand the full capacity of its first Memphis data center, more than 300 MW and 220,000 Nvidia GPUs, to Claude developer Anthropic. Here is what the deal involves and how it connects to Tesla.

t: Tesla can now sell electricity to British homes
d: Ofgem has given Tesla a licence to supply electricity to households and businesses in England, Scotland and Wales. There is no launch date or tariff yet, but the model is likely to follow Tesla Electric in Texas.

t: US Model 3s now get a 16-inch screen
d: Every Model 3 sold in the US, Puerto Rico and Mexico now gets a larger, sharper 16-inch touchscreen. The Performance gains power and range, and the Premium AWD drops to 3.8 seconds from 0 to 60 mph, with prices unchanged.

t: Tesla pressed RDW to soften its FSD review
d: A Reuters investigation based on hundreds of pages of emails says Tesla pressed the RDW over deadlines, test procedures and a €365,000 bill before the Dutch approved FSD Supervised. The RDW says its assessment stayed independent.

t: Apollo Power orders 260 Megapacks for data centers
d: Taiwanese energy company Apollo Power has signed a deal for 260 Megapack 2XL units with Tesla's Taiwan arm. The batteries will serve factories, hospitals, science parks and AI data centers, with deliveries through 2027.

t: SpaceX wants 80000 US towers for Starlink Mobile
d: SpaceX is reportedly negotiating access to tens of thousands of cell sites, while the big carriers try to limit new satellite-to-phone rules. What it means for the networks Tesla cars depend on.

t: Nvidia's new DSX Ready program qualifies Tesla Megapack
d: Nvidia has launched DSX Ready, a qualification program for power and cooling gear in AI data centers. Tesla's Megapack 2XL is one of the first three battery systems on the list. Here is what that means and what it does not.

t: SpaceXAI will become SpaceXSI
d: Elon Musk says SpaceX's AI division will be renamed SpaceXSI, short for SpaceX Super Intelligence. There is no timeline yet. Here is why it is happening and what, if anything, changes for Tesla owners.

t: Crew-13 reaches the station in about eight hours
d: Four astronauts launched on SpaceX's Crew Dragon Grace on October 1 and docked with the ISS in record time for NASA. As on every NASA crew flight with SpaceX since 2020, they rode to the rocket in Tesla cars.

t: 1.3 billion SpaceX shares can now be sold
d: Two trading days after its Q3 results, SpaceX's largest lock-up release lets employees and early investors sell up to 1.3 billion shares. Here is how the schedule works, what comes next and how it ties into the Tesla merger talks.

t: A few 2026 incentives for Tesla buyers remain
d: The US credit is gone and the UK grant excludes Tesla, but Germany now pays up to €6,000 and Dutch tax breaks are shrinking. A country-by-country guide for anyone buying a Tesla in 2026.

t: Energy chief Mike Snyder leaves after 12 years
d: Mike Snyder, the executive who built up Tesla's Megapack business, has stepped down as vice president of energy and charging, according to the Wall Street Journal. Here is who he was, who replaces him and why the timing matters.

t: Musk is Tesla's CEO and not its chairman
d: Musk is Tesla's CEO and largest shareholder, yet he has not chaired the board since 2018 and takes no salary. What his titles mean, the job conditions in his pay awards, and his many other roles.

t: Tesla's solar plant wins long-term Texas tax breaks
d: Texas county commissioners voted 4-0 for a 10-year abatement and long rebates for Project Crystal Sun. Tesla still has not picked the site, and the state must sign off.

t: Finance chief Palani leaves after 17 years
d: Sendil Palani, who joined Tesla when the company was close to collapse in 2008, has announced he is leaving. His exit follows a string of departures of long-serving executives over the past year.

t: Vegas Loop carries 82000 riders during CONEXPO
d: The Boring Company's Las Vegas tunnels moved about 82,000 passengers during the five-day CONEXPO-CON/AGG trade show, and its Prufrock-2 machine completed the longest single Vegas Loop tunnel so far.

t: Starlink passes 10000 satellites in orbit
d: A Falcon 9 launch from California on March 16 pushed SpaceX's Starlink constellation past 10,000 working satellites in orbit at once, less than seven years after the first batch.

t: NHTSA escalates the FSD low-visibility probe
d: US safety regulator NHTSA has upgraded its investigation into how Full Self-Driving handles poor visibility to an engineering analysis, the last step before a possible recall. Here is what it found so far.

t: All 11 xAI co-founders have now left
d: With Ross Nordeen and Manuel Kroiss gone, none of the researchers who founded xAI with Elon Musk in 2023 remain. Tesla has $2 billion and its in-car assistant riding on the outcome.

t: Some Teslas now escape Britain's luxury-car tax
d: From April 1, 2026, electric cars only pay the UK's expensive car supplement above a £50,000 list price. Here are the new rates, which Model 3 and Model Y versions benefit, and what to check on your own car.

t: Netherlands is first in Europe to approve FSD
d: Dutch regulator RDW has approved Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) after more than 18 months of testing. It is valid in the Netherlands only for now, and the driver stays fully responsible.

t: Delaware throws out three Tesla shareholder suits
d: A Delaware judge has dismissed three derivative lawsuits over insider trading, AI and Twitter claims, enforcing the Texas forum rule Tesla adopted when it left Delaware.

t: Tesla Robotaxi expands to Dallas and Houston
d: Tesla has started its Robotaxi service in Dallas and Houston, the first expansion beyond Austin and the Bay Area. The service areas are small and Tesla shared few details, but the cars run with nobody in the driver's seat.

t: Musk's 158 billion pay package paid him nothing
d: Tesla's new filing values Elon Musk's 2025 pay at a record $158 billion, almost all of it accounting value for awards he has not earned. Here is what the number means, and what else the filing showed.

t: Starship V3 flies for the first time
d: SpaceX's first third-generation Starship launched from a new pad in Texas, deployed 22 dummy satellites and splashed down in the Indian Ocean. The Super Heavy booster failed to relight its engines.

t: Tesla signs 25 GWh Megapack deal with NatPower
d: Developer NatPower has agreed a multi-year deal with Tesla for more than 25 GWh of battery storage across five sites in Britain and Italy, worth an estimated $4-5 billion to build. It is one of the largest storage orders ever announced in Europe.

t: Tesla settles the first known FSD pedestrian death
d: Tesla has quietly settled the lawsuit over a 2023 Arizona crash in which a Model Y using Full Self-Driving killed a 71-year-old woman. The terms are secret, but the federal safety probe it started continues.

t: Tesla settles the Optimus trade-secret lawsuit
d: Tesla has dropped its case against former Optimus engineer Jay Li and his startup Proception after a confidential settlement. The same day, Proception announced an $11 million seed round for its robot hands.

t: Tesla delivers 480126 cars in Q2 2026
d: Tesla's second-quarter deliveries jumped 25% from a year earlier to 480,126, ending a two-year run of falling sales and beating analyst expectations by about 74,000 cars. Energy storage reached 13.5 GWh.

t: Frontier's owner picks Starlink for over 1000 planes
d: Indigo Partners, which owns Frontier, Wizz Air, Volaris, JetSMART and Cebu Pacific, will fit Starlink to more than 1,000 aircraft. The first Frontier planes are due in early 2027.

t: Europe's FSD report lists six collisions
d: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) was 5.2 times safer than manual driving across five EU countries. Here are the numbers behind the claim, how they compare, and what they cannot tell us yet.

t: Tesla builds its 10 millionth car in Fremont
d: A Diamond Black Model Y from the Fremont Factory in California is Tesla's 10 millionth vehicle. The first million took 12 years; the next nine million took just over six.

t: China Teslas get local chatbots instead of Grok
d: A new software update brings a Chinese-built AI assistant to Tesla's main models in China. In the rest of the world, the same job is done by Grok from Musk's own AI company.

t: SpaceX closes its 60 billion dollar Cursor deal
d: SpaceX has completed its all-stock takeover of Cursor, the maker of a popular AI coding assistant. The team will now work on Grok, the assistant in Tesla's cars.

t: Clark County approves 19 more Vegas Loop stations
d: The Boring Company now has county approval for 123 Vegas Loop stations, including new stops at F1's Grand Prix Plaza, on Tropicana Avenue and in Chinatown. About 11 are open today.

t: XPeng's IRON robot gets an automated factory line
d: Chinese EV maker XPeng has opened a dedicated production line for its IRON humanoid robot and wants mass production by the end of 2026. That puts it on a similar timeline to Tesla's Optimus.

t: Belgium has started its biggest Megapack battery
d: GIGA Storage has started building a 700 MW / 2.8 GWh battery park in Dilsen-Stokkem, with Tesla supplying the Megapack 3 units and acting as main contractor. Commissioning is planned for spring 2028.

t: Cybertruck now backs up homes with Powerwall 3
d: After more than a year of delays, Tesla's Powershare now lets a Cybertruck feed a home alongside a Powerwall 3 during a power cut. Here is how it works, what you need and what is still missing.

t: Tesla app 4.61 adds sign-in with passkeys
d: The latest Tesla app quietly adds passkey sign-in, a safer alternative to passwords, plus live Supercharger site maps on iPhone. Here is what is new and how to set up a passkey in five steps.

t: Musk proposes a 200 mph San Antonio tunnel
d: Elon Musk says The Boring Company is working on a tunnel linking Austin and San Antonio, with trips of under 30 minutes. There is no route, budget or permit yet. Here is what was said, and the Tesla link.

t: Starship reaches orbit and releases 26 satellites
d: On Flight 14, SpaceX's Starship lost an engine on the way up, still made it to orbit, deployed its first real satellites and came down early near Hawaii. Here is what happened and why it matters for Tesla.

t: Emergency Drive Away leaves the cable plugged in
d: A new software feature in update 2026.38.3 lets Tesla drivers in the US shift into Drive while connected to a Supercharger, for emergencies only. Here is how it works, what it costs, and why Tesla added it.

t: Giga Shanghai now exports nearly half its cars
d: Tesla's Shanghai plant sold 95,366 cars in September, its best month of 2026, and a record 275,111 in the third quarter. Exports have more than doubled this year while sales in China keep falling.

t: Tesla drops the 'Full Self-Driving' name in Europe
d: Under pressure from European regulators who called the name misleading, Tesla has renamed Full Self-Driving to Tesla Assisted Driving on its European websites. The US keeps the old name.

t: NHTSA reviews Robotaxi speeding claims near schools
d: US safety regulators have opened a defect petition review after a complaint that Tesla's driverless Robotaxis ignore lower speed limits in active school zones. No crashes or injuries are reported, but a formal investigation is possible.

t: Flex Connect can open Superchargers two years early
d: Tesla says a flexible grid connection with California utility PG&E lets new Supercharger sites open more than two years earlier. Here is how it works, and what it means for drivers.

t: Tesla slips under half of America's fast chargers
d: A new Paren report shows Tesla's share of US DC fast-charging ports fell below half in Q3 2026, even though Tesla still builds more chargers than anyone else. Here are the numbers and what they mean for drivers.

t: A driver says he slept with FSD engaged
d: A Tesla drove through a closed section of Interstate 80 in California and crashed into a parked Highway Patrol car. The driver told officers he had fallen asleep with Full Self-Driving engaged. CHP released dashcam video on Thursday.

t: SpaceX will try to catch Starship itself
d: On its third-quarter call, SpaceX confirmed that Flight 15 will try to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Starship upper stage with the launch tower. Here is what we know.

t: The Tesla app finally gets a tablet layout
d: Tesla is rolling out a redesigned app for iPads, Android tablets, foldables and Apple's new iPhone Duo, with a split-screen menu and a large 3D car view. Here is what changes and when you get it.

t: Robotaxis logged 3.1 million miles without injuries
d: Tesla has published its first Robotaxi safety report, claiming 3.1 million miles without a safety monitor and no injuries. It also names Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio as the next cities. Here is what the numbers show, and what they leave out.

t: Warranty terms differ across the US and Europe
d: Four years for the car, eight for the battery, and different mileage limits on each side of the Atlantic. A plain guide to Tesla's warranties, the 70% battery promise, used-car cover and your legal rights in Europe.

t: Nine directors sit on Tesla's 2026 board
d: Tesla's board decides on Elon Musk's pay and the SpaceX merger question. Here is who the nine directors are, which links Tesla considers harmless, and why critics still question the board's independence.

t: Here is the servicing a Tesla actually needs
d: No oil changes and no mandatory annual service, but tyres, filters, brake fluid and brakes still need attention. Tesla's recommended intervals for Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, in plain language.

t: Six habits can lower a Supercharger bill
d: Supercharger prices in the US have crept up this year, with big differences between states and between members and non-members. Here is what a charge costs now, and how to keep the bill down.

t: Optimus went from a 2021 reveal toward production
d: Five years ago Optimus was an idea on a stage. Now Tesla says it is building production-quality robots in Fremont. A clear timeline of every key step, promise and delay.

t: Starlink leads Amazon Leo by a wide margin
d: Starlink has about 11,100 satellites and 13.6 million subscribers. Amazon's Leo has fewer than 400 satellites and has not launched service yet. Here is how the two compare, and why it matters for Tesla.

t: Three Megafactories hold 110 GWh of capacity
d: Tesla now builds its Megapack grid batteries in three dedicated plants on two continents. Here is what each one does, how big they are and why the network matters.

t: Sentry Mode watches your Tesla and uses battery
d: Sentry Mode turns a parked Tesla into a security camera. Here is how it works, what USB drive you need, how much range it costs per day, and why the rules are stricter in Europe.

t: Tesla discloses every deal with Musk's other firms
d: Megapacks for xAI, Cybertrucks for SpaceX, ads on X and a $2 billion SpaceX stake: Tesla's proxy statement lists what it bought from and sold to companies linked to Elon Musk and its directors.

t: A Tesla can test its own battery health
d: Teslas can now measure their own battery health. A step-by-step guide to running the test, reading the percentage, and the charging habits Tesla recommends to keep your battery healthy.

t: Powerwall 3 and 3P suit different houses
d: Tesla now sells two versions of its home battery: the single-phase Powerwall 3 and the three-phase Powerwall 3P for Europe. Here is how they differ in power, solar inputs and backup, and which one suits which home.

t: Tesla's plug is now the SAE J3400 standard
d: Tesla's charging plug is now the North American standard, known officially as SAE J3400. Here is how that happened, what the plug can do, which brands can Supercharge, and why none of this applies in Europe.

t: A report warns of sinkholes under downtown Nashville
d: The Boring Company's tunnel under Nashville has reached the Music City Center. A hydrogeology report says the hardest limestone, with caves and contaminated sites nearby, is still to come.

t: Here is how a Tesla Robotaxi ride works
d: Planning to try a driverless Tesla? Here is a practical guide to the Robotaxi app, where the service runs, what a ride costs, how the Cybercab differs from a Model Y, and the limits to know before you go.

t: Tesla trains Optimus with cameras worn by people
d: Tesla teaches its humanoid robot mostly by filming people at work, not by steering it remotely. Here is how the method works, how it changed, and where it still falls short.

t: Starlink beams internet from satellites to a dish
d: A plain-language guide to how SpaceX's Starlink gets internet from space to your home, phone or car, why it is faster than older satellite services, and what that means for Tesla.

t: Other companies process Grok chats from your Tesla
d: Grok conversations in a Tesla are handled by SpaceX's AI division, not by Tesla. Here is what Tesla says about anonymity, location and contacts, and which cars and connections you need.

t: Buffalo now builds Supercharger parts and solar panels
d: Tesla's Buffalo plant was meant to be a giant solar factory. Today it makes Supercharger parts and energy products, assembles a new solar panel and labels data for FSD. Here is how it got there.

t: Cybertruck and Starship share one stainless alloy
d: Tesla's pickup and SpaceX's rocket share more than an owner. Both use cold-worked stainless steel developed by a materials team that worked for both companies. Here is how that came about.

t: One winning city quit the free-tunnel offer
d: In March, The Boring Company picked three cities for a free one-mile Loop tunnel. One winner pulled out a day later. Here is where the New Orleans and Dallas projects stand.

t: SpaceXAI's model sprint now reaches Grok 5
d: SpaceX's AI division shipped three Grok models in ten weeks and wants Grok 5 by year-end. What changed, what it means for Grok in Tesla cars, and why Optimus depends on it too.

t: Musk owns 19.8% of Tesla
d: Tesla's new proxy statement puts Elon Musk's stake at almost 700 million shares, or 19.8%. Here is what that number includes, what it leaves out, and why it matters.

t: Tesla insurance stays expensive for several reasons
d: Teslas are often expensive to insure. Here is why, what Tesla's own driving-score insurance offers in the US, and practical steps that lower the premium on both sides of the Atlantic.

t: Macrohard is the Digital Optimus software project
d: Musk's 'Digital Optimus' is meant to do office work on Tesla's AI4 chip with Grok as the brain. What the joint project is, why it matters for Tesla, and why there is still no product.

t: Starship misses the 2026 Mars window
d: Musk once promised Starship would leave for Mars at the end of 2026 with Tesla's Optimus on board. That window is here and no rocket is going. What changed, and what it means for Optimus.

t: Six-seat Model Y L leads Korean imports
d: The stretched, six-seat Model Y L accounted for 70% of Tesla's 12,372 registrations in South Korea in September, making it the country's most popular imported car by a wide margin.

t: Musk's 2018 pay fight lasted eight years
d: A shareholder with nine Tesla shares sued in 2018. Eight years later Musk has exercised the options, Tesla got $1 in damages and the company has moved to Texas. The full timeline.

t: Starlink switched on free service after disasters
d: Starlink offered free service after Hurricane Lowell and the Colombia earthquake, and now has a disaster deal with the US State Department. How it works, and how Cybertrucks and Tesla batteries have joined in.

t: Tesla Automations will add routines to your car
d: A finished English version of Tesla's Automations app has been found hidden in current software. Here is what the routine builder can do, what it can't, and when it could arrive.

t: Tesla's own battery plants are still a bottleneck
d: Battery supply is still the limit on how many cars Tesla can build. Its new cell and materials plants in Nevada and Texas are in early ramp. Here is what each one makes, how big it is and how far along it is.

t: Tesla wins its appeal against the FSD class
d: A federal appeals court has thrown out the class certification in LoSavio v. Tesla, the long-running case over Tesla's claim that its cars had the hardware for full self-driving. The lawsuit itself continues.

t: Three in four new Teslas now include FSD
d: More than 75% of Tesla's Q3 deliveries in North America included FSD, and active users hit a record 1.74 million. Here is what changed, what the numbers mean, and how far Tesla is from its 10 million goal.

t: The hand remains the hardest part of Optimus
d: Tesla says the hand and forearm are harder to build than the rest of its humanoid robot. A new patent filing shows how Tesla wants to give Optimus a sense of touch, and why the hand decides whether the robot is useful.

t: Powerwalls sent a record 601 MW into California
d: On October 6, Tesla's California virtual power plant delivered 601 MW and 932 MWh from home batteries, its biggest event yet. Together with Sunrun, home batteries supplied 745 MW. Here is how it works and what owners get paid.

t: Tariff refunds added 447 million to Q3 profit
d: Tesla's quarterly filing reveals $786 million in US tariff refunds booked in Q3 2026, partly passed on to Megapack customers. Without them, the energy margin was closer to 24% than 33%.

t: Just one in 200 Supercharger drivers waits
